purpose: same-problem method competition plus paper-code consistency learning

Q1.S003: adaptive three-stage sliding-window narrative, but printed code is fixed-window diff
Q1.selection_rule: Use exact batch rainflow as gold standard; prefer an explicitly stateful online algorithm or a window approximation only after nonnegative increment/boundary-cycle tests and runtime-fidelity benchmarking.

Q2.S003: segmented high-order physics-inspired nonlinear regression + random search
Q2.selection_rule: Start with unit-consistent low-parameter physics/residual models; upgrade complexity only if chronological/group holdout demonstrates gain. Do not mix standardized variables directly with raw-unit physical equations.

Q3.S003: Pareto/regional/MPC narrative + SLSQP, but printed code collapses to static per-second optimization
Q3.selection_rule: Use an explicit solver as interpretable benchmark. Call a method MPC only when horizon, dynamics/forecast, rolling execution and cross-time constraints are all implemented; call a method Pareto only when a front and operating-point rule are actually produced.

Q4.S002: SVD denoise + phase delay + spline reconstruction
Q4.S003: Kalman + delay compensation + robust MPC/PSO narrative
Q4.selection_rule: Separate corruption identification, preprocessing/state estimation, and downstream optimization. Validate each stage independently and sweep noise/delay severity.

new_consistency_checks: named algorithm vs executable call graph
figure_design_lesson: S003 has 42 captioned figures but no actual numbered Pareto-front figure despite Pareto being central; figure count is secondary to whether each central claim has direct evidence.
